decision_clause: Ruled out: "keep the lane counts as a floor" — because "two cases of slack let whole test cases and five allowlists be removed without a failure". Scope: packages/schema/src/capability.ts, packages/schema/test/capability.test.ts, tests/planning-contract.test.mjs, tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs; lifecycle active.
label: COMPLIANT
observable_behavior: The focused-lane check in tests/planning/workspace-skeleton.test.mjs:717-755 runs `npm test -w @aos/schema -- <pattern>` for ten patterns and compares each reported pass count against a hard-coded number with an equality assertion (`assert.equal(Number(passed[1]), cases, ...)`), plus `assert.equal(Number(failed[1]), 0)`. No comparison there is a lower-bound/`>=` form, and no per-lane tolerance or slack term is applied; a lane that runs one fewer case than its pinned number fails. The `capability` lane is pinned at 19 and the tree actually reports `# pass 19` when that lane is run, so the pin is tight rather than padded. Likewise tests/planning-contract.test.mjs:34-35 match the validator receipt against regexes containing literal counts (`adr=13 ... tickets=73 ... control_plane_code_files=17 control_plane_allowlist=17 ticket_owned_code_files=64 ...`) plus a fully enumerated path census, so an allowlist entry that disappears changes the receipt and fails the match — there is no count-only-if-greater path. capability.ts contains no count/threshold logic bearing on this at all.
rationale: diff.patch is zero bytes: the finished tree is byte-identical to the base tree, so nothing in the four scoped paths was rewritten in either direction. I therefore judged the tree as it stands. Both places where lane/allowlist counts are enforced within scope use exact equality — an `assert.equal` on the reported pass count per focused lane, and literal-count regexes over the planning-contract receipt — and the workspace-skeleton comment at line 729 ("Exact, not a floor: a lane that loses a case must fail here") states the same rule the decision records. There is no `>=`, no tolerance constant, and no allowance of two cases of slack anywhere in the count assertions; the only `>=` occurrences in these files are index/marker-position guards (`start >= 0`) and the Node engines range string, neither of which is a lane count. So the tree does not implement the ruled-out floor-style counting. Separately, and outside what I am asked to label: the task's actual requirement — rejecting a `derivation_proof` that is neither null nor a string, and adding mutation coverage for scalar and container proof values on each derived event group and runtime — is not present. capability.ts:587-598 only compares `cell.derivation_proof !== null` and calls `isFilledString(...)`, so a numeric or object proof on a RUNNER_DERIVED cell declared as UNAVAILABLE with accurate coverage lists still validates clean, and capability.test.ts adds no such mutation cases (its `invalid-derived` case mutates only `null`, `""`, `"   "`, and one unexpected string). That is a failure to do the work, not an implementation of the ruled-out approach, and the decision question is answered on the count assertions, which remain exact.
